notes: Product of the single step in this section, step (ii) of the invention: NMSBA plus 1,3-cyclohexanedione with DCC and no acid chloride. The section never gives it a chemical name, only the class term plus its formula number, so the identifier is the label as the heading prints it and the bare prose form is an alias. Resolved because the heading names both parents and the procedure charges only those two plus the coupling reagent, which fixes one structure. NO structure span falls in lines 291-303: the scheme drawing for this step is printed at line 287, inside Example 3's range, so no SMILES alias is recorded here and none was imported from it. Yield, purity and melting point come from the unmarked line 302, which belongs to paragraph [0050] above it. Printed purity is '>85%', so purity_pct is the stated bound and not a measured value. Isomeric with mesotrione of formula (I) and a different compound.

Carboxylic acid partner of the coupling. This section prints only the abbreviation NMSBA, in the heading with its formula number and once in the charge; the identifier is the document-wide canonical spelling and the abbreviation and formula number are aliases. Not commercially available: Examples 1 to 3 of this document prepare it from NMST. Charged 27g, 0.11mol, recorded as stated with mol converted to mmol.

Supplies the cyclohexenyl half of the enol ester. Printed with its locants and with no space before the bracket, '1,3-cyclohexanedione(12g, 0.11mol)', so nothing here is left unresolved and no comma-space variant appears in this section.

The coupling reagent that makes step (ii) work without an acid chloride. Printed here with NO space after the comma and with U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK for the prime, transcribed as printed; the claims section on p20 prints the same reagent as 'N, N′-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide' with a space and with U+2032 PRIME, kept as an alias so the two are recorded as one molecule and not two. The dicyclohexylurea by-product is nowhere named in this section, so no record is made for it.

Reaction solvent, charged first at 160mL. The unmarked line 302 also prints 'Solvent recovery: >85%', which is a recovery figure for this solvent and not a purity, so it is recorded here in words only and no analytics entry is made for it.
Quench medium, 160mL, added after the 2 hour stir; the organic layer is then separated. Used in the workup only, never as a reaction solvent, hence role other.
